subject: Little confusion about comparing latent variable means (mean structure)

messages.author: a3e8ab9ab5e51bfc
messages.subject: Little confusion about comparing latent variable means (mean structure)
parts:
Hello everyone,

so I have an hypothesis that states that my latent variable means (measured with four indicators) differs between (two) groups and that the mean in the second group is higher than the one in the lower group.

So I have read that the basic way to do this would be by specifying the following model (after I already assumed factor loadings to be equal):

model <- '# measurement model 1
factor =~ 1*a + b + c

fit <- cfa(model, data=data, group = "group",
            group.equal =c("loadings","intercepts"))

this gives me the following intercept parameter for the second group:

                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
    factor           -0.345    0.035   -9.983    0.000   -0.452   -0.452

so from this, can I say that the factor mean is lower in the second group than in the first group?

Is that all I have to do to test my hypothesis?

Now, I have also read about specifying mean structures, which confused me. It seems like the sort of hypothesis I want to test needs a mean structure to be specified by adding "meanstructure = TRUE", is that correct? If so, what exactly would that change?

Reference:
http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/means.html

messages.author: 90e03273c83a92f7
messages.subject: Re: Little confusion about comparing latent variable means (mean structure)
parts:
Don't you think you should see if your model even fits? There are many fit statistics you can look at. 

You should also consider progressively making the model more strict, like just do configural first (remove equal loadings and intercepts), then try metric equivalence (only set the loadings equal), then run an anova() and see if metric equivalence model is a significantly worse fit than your configural equivalence model. Then you can try the same with the model where both loadings and intercepts are equal. But check the fit indices too.

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Little confusion about comparing latent variable means (mean structure)
parts:
Hi

The method if after getting strong invariance between groups, you do a null hypothesis test of equality of latent means between groups.

Basically you compare (chi-square difference test) a model where the latent means are different between groups, and another model where the latent means are equal across groups. The chi-square test is just another null hypothesis, with the null: no difference between groups

I am attaching an R file that is a full example of multiple group CFA, invariance and latent parameter testing. The comments are in spanish, for a workshop I gave a couple years ago

-- Mauricio
